s1.syndrome_frame: bilateral breast lumps with suspicious masses and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: left breast lump fixed to the chest wall
irregular spiculated mass in the left breast on MRI
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
regular menstrual cycles
left breast lump 4 × 4 cm hard and fixed to the chest wall
right breast lump 1 × 1 cm firm and mobile
MRI showed irregular spiculated mass in the left breast
MRI showed well-defined lesion in the right breast
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy on MRI
ultrasound and bone scan negative for metastases
fine-needle aspiration cytology of left breast lump showed malignant cells
FNAC of left axillary lymph node showed malignant cells
core-needle biopsy of left breast confirmed infiltrative duct cell carcinoma
estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive

raw.syndrome_frame: bilateral breast lumps with suspicious masses and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: left breast lump fixed to the chest wall
irregular spiculated mass in the left breast on MRI
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
regular menstrual cycles
left breast lump 4 × 4 cm hard and fixed to the chest wall
right breast lump 1 × 1 cm firm and mobile
MRI showed irregular spiculated mass in the left breast
MRI showed well-defined lesion in the right breast
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy on MRI
ultrasound and bone scan negative for metastases
fine-needle aspiration cytology of left breast lump showed malignant cells
FNAC of left axillary lymph node showed malignant cells
core-needle biopsy of left breast confirmed infiltrative duct cell carcinoma
estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive

differentials: squamous cell carcinoma of the breast
per_call: squamous cell carcinoma of the breast

shortlist.label: invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: confirmed by core-needle biopsy and FNAC of left breast lump

shortlist.label: inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral breast lumps and lymphadenopathy, although no classic signs of inflammation

shortlist.label: lobular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral involvement, although invasive ductal carcinoma is more common

shortlist.label: medullary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism and prominent nucleoli on FNAC

shortlist.label: lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy, although primary breast lymphoma is rare

raw.rationale: The presence of a hard, fixed lump in the left breast, irregular spiculated mass on MRI, and malignant cells on fine-needle aspiration cytology and core-needle biopsy are consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma. The tumor's estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive status further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of skin changes or inflammation typical of inflammatory breast cancer

rejected.label: lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: The presence of a hard, fixed lump and the description of the malignant cells do not specifically suggest lobular carcinoma

rejected.label: medullary carcinoma
rejected.why: The description of the tumor and the presence of estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive status do not align with medullary carcinoma, which is typically triple-negative

rejected.label: lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings are not consistent with lymphoma, and the biopsy results confirm a carcinoma
